title: Gaussian logarithmic Sobolev inequality
statement:
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ belong to Gaussian $L^2$. For $t>0$, define the Gaussian noise average $T_t f(x)=\int f(e^{-t}x+\sqrt{1-e^{-2t}}y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$. Suppose that $(f-T_t f)/t$ converges to $g$ in Gaussian $L^2$ as $t\to0^+$. Then $f^2\log(f^2)$ is Gaussian integrable, and, writing $\operatorname{Ent}_{\gamma_n}(h)=\int h\log h\,d\gamma_n-(\int h\,d\gamma_n)\log(\int h\,d\gamma_n)$, one has
\[
\operatorname{Ent}_{\gamma_n}(f^2)\le 2\int fg\,d\gamma_n.
\]
hypotheses_covered: $(f-T_t f)/t$ converges to $g$ in Gaussian $L^2$ as $t\to0^+$
